To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TiN/ Al2O3/ Pt device is more stable than the Ti/AlO3/ Pt one for nonvolatile memory application.
the influence of the top electrode on the forming and switching behaviors of the resistive random access memories with various compliance currents has been studied and compared.

the Ti/Al 2O 3/Pt device shows a lower forming voltage and a higher initial intermediate state probability, but its RS parameters such as Vset/Vreset, RHRS/RLRS (measured with 0.10 V), and resistance ratio are similar to those of the TiN/ Al 2O 2/Pt device.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of top electrodes on the electrical switching behaviors of the Ti/AlOx/Pt and TiO2/Pt RRAMs.
the influence of the top electrode on the switching characteristics of the Al2OX/Pt RRAM device with various CCs.
the influence of the top electrode on the RS behaviors and the conduction mechanisms of Al2O3-based RRAM devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ti/AlO3/Pt devices have the advantage of lower forming voltage but the TiN/ALO3/Pt has the advantage of better stability.
Ti/Al2 O 3/Pt device with the intermediate state has the lower forming voltage and the TiN/ Al 2O 3/Pt devices with the isolated state has the better stability.
the TiN/ Al2O3 /Pt device is better than the Ti/Al 2 O 3 /Pt device in RS characteristics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TiN/ Al2O3/ Pt RRAM device is more stable than the Ti/Al 2O3/P t RRAM device with the modulation of CCs and the application of the stop voltage.
TiN/AlO3/Pt is a better choice than Ti/Al2OX/Pt as the RRAM device.
the Ti/AlOx/Pt and Ti/Al2 O3/Pt RRS devices have similar switching characteristics with the TiN/ Al2O3/ Pt device.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the top electrode material has an influence on the RS behaviors of the RRAM devices.
the TiN/ Al2O3/ Pt device is a better candidate to achieve the high-performance resistive random access memories.
TiN is a better top electrode material than Ti, especially for the Al2O 3-based RRAM devices with a high CC.
